facts.fact: StackAdapt's author states there are 5 standard campaign reports: Geo, Device, Domain, Creative and Audience.
facts.quote: In StackAdapt, there are 5 standard reports I always go back to: Geo, Device, Domain, Creative and Audience.

facts.fact: In the author's example e-commerce travel conversion campaign, the 970×250 creative (Example 4.2) drove an eCPC of $0.89 and an eCPA of $10.06, which the author describes as the most cost-efficient user engagement performance.
facts.quote: This creative is responsible for driving the most cost efficient performance related to user engagement, accounting for a $0.89 eCPC and $10.06 eCPA.

facts.fact: In the author's example campaign, the 300×600 creative (Example 1.1) generated only 1 conversion and had the highest eCPA achieved.
facts.quote: Generating only 1 conversion, this creative accounts for the highest eCPA achieved.

facts.fact: In the author's example campaign, the 160×600 creative (Example 3.1) achieved 0 conversions while having the most expensive eCPM and eCPC.
facts.quote: With 0 conversions achieved, along with the most expensive eCPM and eCPC, recommend pausing this creative from serving.

facts.fact: The StackAdapt blog post was published on 2019-10-17.
StackAdapt's Insights tool lets users pause or enable campaign targeting directly from the report, according to the vendor.
facts.quote: you’re able to pause or enable campaign targeting directly from the report!

facts.fact: According to the vendor, scheduled reporting can be set up before a campaign launches so data is emailed automatically.
facts.quote: you can set up scheduled reporting ahead of time.
